title: Trace linking and per-route cost attribution for embeddings + rerank observability
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Customers and internal SREs cannot reliably attribute latency or USD cost to an upstream API route that uses the embeddings + reranking pipeline. Traces are often fragmented across async workers/batches and the cost model undercounts per-route token usage when requests are co-batched or served from KV cache. Goals: (1) maintain a single trace id across request lifecycle (ingest -> embedding worker -> vector search -> reranker -> response), (2) emit per-route metrics that break down latency and estimated cost by embedding vs. rerank tokens and cached hits, and (3) ship Grafana dashboards + SLO/alerting for regressions and cost spikes.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end trace can be followed from API gateway to final HTTP response for 95% of sampled requests (OTel span linking across queue/batch boundaries).
Dashboard: per-route card showing P50/P95 latency, p95 rerank time, embedding time, batch size histogram, and estimated cost per-request in USD.
Cost attribution: computed per-route cost estimates agree with billing simulation within 5% over a 24h test window.
Alerts: automated alert when route-level P95 latency increases >30% vs baseline OR cost-per-request spikes >40% vs 24h baseline. Alerts route to #sre and responsible PM.
Integration tests: synthetic harness generates traces and validates that trace id propagation and cost tags are present for 99% of synthetic events.
technical_notes: Tracing: use OTel propagation with explicit parent_trace_id propagated in message headers and stored on batch/worker jobs. Add span attributes: route.name, model.name, model.version, batch_id, batch_origin_trace_id.

Metrics: expose Prometheus metrics tagged by route and model: embeddings_calls_total, rerank_calls_total, tokens_generated_total, kv_cache_hits_total, batch_size_distribution, estimated_cost_usd_total, estimated_cost_usd_per_request.

Cost model: reuse existing per-token microcosts in billing service but apply allocation heuristics for shared batches: attribute cost to routes by token share within batch, with an opt-in experimental 'batch-origin attribution' flag. Document tradeoffs (small variance vs precision).
Storage: time series retained in Cortex/Prometheus for 90d for dashboarding; traces stored in Tempo/OTel for 30d.
Performance: avoid adding blocking IPC on hot path. Propagate trace ids async and annotate batch metadata once; sampling set at 1% by default for production, 100% in canary/test.
implementation_plan: Spike (2d): implement trace header passthrough in SDK + simple worker instrumentation; verify end-to-end in dev cluster.
Instrument batching layer (3d): tag each batch with originating trace ids list and primary_origin; emit metrics about batch composition and size; add batch_id span.
Cost attribution (2d): implement shared-batch allocation logic in metrics collector and a feature flag to enable experimental allocation.
Dashboards (2d): Grafana per-route dashboard template (P50/P95 latency, cost breakdown, batch size, kv cache hit rate, traces link).
Alerts & SLOs (1d): add Prometheus alert rules and SLO burn rate alerts; integrate with PagerDuty and #sre Slack channel.
Canary rollout (3d): enable on staging for selected high-volume routes, run synthetic traffic, validate accuracy and no performance regressions, then roll to 10% prod and 100% after signoff.
qa_plan: Synthetic harness: 3 scenarios (single small request, high-batch-mixed-tenant, KV cache-hit heavy) running for 24h with known token counts to validate cost attribution and trace links.
Regression tests: latency microbench for embedding handler + batch annotation to ensure <1% added p95 latency overhead in hot path.
Manual review: PM + SRE inspect dashboard and 5 sample traces per scenario to confirm span continuity and correct attributes.
Load test: 5k QPS synthetic workload with mixed request sizes to verify metrics cardinality and Prometheus scrape stability.
rollout_notes: Feature flag: observability.embeddings.rerank.trace_linking (off by default). Use canary to flip for targeted routes.
Gradual ramp: dev -> staging -> canary 10% -> 100%. Monitor latency, CPU on worker hosts, and Prometheus cardinality.
Fallback: if noise or cardinality explosion observed, revert flag and revert collector changes; have script to aggregate metrics by sampling.
comments: 2026-02-16 Maya Chen: Kickoff meeting notes added to Confluence. Agreed on using OTel and keeping sampling low for prod. Action: Ravi to spike trace propagation.

2026-02-20 Ravi Patel: Spike complete. Basic trace header passthrough working in dev. Observed that batching loses original request trace id when worker aggregates multiple headers; proposing primary_origin and origins_count scheme.

2026-02-25 SRE review (Anika Gomez): Recommended tagging batch with primary_origin and a compressed fingerprint of origin IDs to avoid high-cardinality. Also asked to cap per-route metric cardinality.
2026-03-02 Design review (Leo Martin): Dashboards should surface 'cost per route per 1k requests' and provide quick links to top-5 traces causing the highest cost. Minor UX feedback incorporated.

2026-03-05 Ravi Patel: Implemented batch_id span and added batch composition metrics (batch_size, origin_count). PR opened: #1834. Requesting eng review for Prometheus label strategy to avoid cardinality blowup.
2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Security okayed non-sensitive trace attributes; ensure no customer PII flows into spans. Add a scrubber to batch metadata.

2026-03-12 Ravi Patel: Canary in staging started on routes: /search/semantic and /kb/query. Initial telemetry looks reasonable; cost estimate drift <3% in 6h smoke. Next: add alert rules and run 24h synthetic test.
